Bernard Vellut : « On veut que ce soit une belle fête »

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 22 min read (4380 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Poteaux-carres

⏱️ ~22 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that À quelques jours du choc face à l’AS Saint-Étienne au Parc des Sports d’Annecy, pour le compte du 7e tour de la Coupe de France, le GFA Rumilly Vallières est en pleine effervescence.
  • Bonjour Bernard Vellut et merci de nous accorder ces quelques minutes d’interview.
  • Effectivement, nous sommes quatre co-présidents.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that À quelques jours du choc face à l’AS Saint-Étienne au Parc des Sports d’Annecy, pour le compte du 7e tour de la Coupe de France, le GFA Rumilly Vallières est en pleine effervescence. Le club haut-savoyard cultive un modèle unique porté par quatre co-présidents et un esprit résolument familial. L'un d'eux, Bernard Vellut (à droite sur la photo), revient pour nous sur les coulisses de cette ascension fulgurante, les défis structurels du club et l'excitation qui entoure la venue des Verts.

Bonjour Bernard Vellut et merci de nous accorder ces quelques minutes d’interview. Le club de Rumilly Vallières a la particularité d'être dirigé par quatre co-présidents avec chacun un rôle dédié. En ce qui te concerne, tu as en charge les instances de football et les collectivités territoriales. Comment est née cette organisation assez unique et comment vous répartissez-vous la charge au quotidien ?

Effectivement, nous sommes quatre co-présidents. Comment cela est-il arrivé ? Moi j'étais président du club de Rumilly et Luc Chabert était président du club de Vallières, à trois kilomètres de chez nous. On a donc évoqué un rapprochement de nos deux clubs, plutôt que de se tirer dans les pattes, sans parler encore de fusion. Mais il y avait toujours quelque chose qui clochait au niveau de détails plus ou moins importants. C'est toujours une question humaine de toute façon.

It has been revealed that À un moment donné, on s’est dit qu'il fallait arrêter de se piquer les joueurs et réfléchir à faire quelque chose de plus grand. Avec Luc Chabert, qui a une très grosse entreprise de fromagerie avec une dizaine de laiteries, on s’est dit : « On y va ! ». On s’est donc réunis une fois, deux fois, trois fois. Au début ça tiquait un petit peu, mais on est arrivés à se dire qu'on allait commencer par tout le cursus jeunes. Les jeunes, eux, c'est d’abord la couleur du maillot, les histoires de personnes ils n’en ont rien à cirer ! On a fait deux années comme ça avec les jeunes et ça a tellement bien marché qu'on a ensuite souhaité fusionner tout le club. De là est née la structure des quatre co-présidents : j'avais un vice-président avec moi et Luc Chabert avait le sien de son côté. On s’est dit qu’on n’allait pas faire d'histoires et qu'à quatre co-présidents, on ne serait pas trop pour gérer le club.

According to recent reports, les choses se sont déroulées de la meilleure des façons. Au-delà de la présidence, on est tous devenus amis, ainsi que nos épouses respectives. Quand tu as quatre co-présidents comme ça qui mènent la barque, tous les gens derrière voient que ça marche super bien et l'engouement est parti. Au niveau de la répartition : Bruno Piccon s'occupe de toute la partie jeunes, Luc Chabert gère les partenaires, François Baudet s'occupe de la communication et du matériel, et pour ma part, je m'occupe des instances, des terrains, de la mairie de Vallières, du district, de la Ligue et de la Fédération. Je fais également partie du comité directeur de la Ligue où je représente les clubs nationaux de la région Rhône-Alpes, ainsi qu'au siège à Paris.

Industry observers note that en dehors de cela, on a tous notre boulot, bien sûr. Toutes les trois semaines, on se réunit et on mange ensemble pour échanger sur les perspectives, les actions en cours ou à venir, et ce qui a été bien ou moins bien fait. Derrière, on a un comité directeur pour décider des orientations dans les différentes commissions, et trois semaines après, ces commissions nous rendent compte de leurs résultats. On avance comme ça, sans compter les coups de téléphone et les messages tous les deux jours... On communique beaucoup ! On est obligés de travailler comme cela maintenant parce qu'on a quand même 800 licenciés, ce n'est pas rien.

Comme tu le disais, le club est né d'une fusion en 2018, et il se retrouve aujourd'hui à une très belle place en championnat (le club est actuellement 2e de sa poule en National 1, à 3 points de Nîmes avec un match de retard, ndp²). Le club a aussi connu une épopée fantastique en Coupe de France en 2021. Quel regard portez-vous sur cette ascension fulgurante et est-ce que le monde professionnel est une ambition ou un doux rêve ?

Sources indicate that on a l'habitude de faire les choses les unes après les autres. Quand on est montés, on voulait voir à quel niveau on pouvait se situer. Aujourd'hui, il ne faut pas se leurrer, les joueurs comme le staff sont pratiquement tous professionnels. Comme nous avons un budget serré, nous souhaitons avancer pas à pas et ne surtout pas brûler les étapes.

It has been revealed that au niveau du coach, nous avons un gars super, Cédric Rullier, qui a essentiellement recruté régionalement. On ne voulait pas recruter trop loin parce que la vie est très chère en Haute-Savoie et qu'il faut se loger. Maintenant qu'on a un niveau honnête avec de l’ambition, on va chercher un petit peu plus loin, mais toujours des joueurs ciblés sur leur mentalité et leur respect. C'est après les qualités sportives bien sûr, mais un joueur qui ne rentre pas dans notre moule mentalement, on ne le prend pas. On veut garder notre esprit familial, même si on s'est beaucoup professionnalisés.

According to recent reports, on a énormément de bénévoles et on veut que la mayonnaise prenne entre eux et les joueurs. C'est ce qui fait notre force aujourd'hui : le groupe vit très bien, l'entraîneur est exceptionnel et les bénévoles sont hyper dévoués. Dès que tu demandes quelque chose, ils sont tous derrière toi pour t'aider. Aujourd'hui, c'est fantastique !

Et la Coupe de France dans tout ça ?

La Coupe de France, cela n’a rien à voir avec le championnat, les émotions sont multipliées par dix ou quinze. En 2021, lors de notre exploit, on a commencé en gagnant aux tirs au but contre un club de district, un truc de dingue. Petit à petit, on a passé les tours : on a sorti Prix-lès-Mézières et le FC Annecy aux tirs au but, puis Le Puy en huitièmes, Toulouse en quarts, avant de tomber contre Monaco en demi-finale. C'était complètement fou.

Le seul bémol, c'est que ça s'est joué pendant le Covid, donc il n'y avait pas de supporters au stade. Mais ça ne nous a pas empêchés de nous retrouver le soir des victoires. La mairie et la gendarmerie ont été très sympas avec nous parce qu'ils savaient qu'ils ne pouvaient pas faire autrement. J'ai une petite anecdote pour le match contre Monaco : le préfet avait donné l'autorisation à deux ou trois équipes de jeunes de nous accompagner à la sortie du restaurant à midi. Sauf qu'on s'est retrouvés à 3 000 dans les rues ! Les gendarmes n'ont rien pu faire, c'était un truc de fou. C'est une expérience qu'on ne reverra peut-être jamais, en tout cas pas moi, mais c'est tout le mal que je souhaite au club.

According to recent reports, depuis, ça fait trois ans qu'on se fait éliminer aux tirs au but. On s'était dit que cette année, il fallait que ça change pour aller chercher un 32e ou un gros club. On n'est pas encore en 32e, on a eu quelques soucis et on est encore passés aux tirs au but au tour précédent. J'ai l'impression que c'est dans la tête : quand tu rencontres une équipe plus faible, tu te mets à son diapason. Mais avec les joueurs qu'on a aujourd'hui, si on tombe contre une équipe plus forte, ils savent hausser leur niveau. On ne lâche rien. Par exemple, hier à Saint-Priest, il y avait 2-2 à un quart d'heure de la fin. On fait rentrer le banc, pouf, on met 4-2, et si le match continue on en met encore deux ou trois. C'est formidable.

Industry observers note that parlons un peu des infrastructures du club et de vos perspectives d'évolution. De quels terrains disposez-vous actuellement ?

On a un terrain en herbe à Rumilly avec un synthétique à côté. Le centre de Vallières est consacré aux jeunes et aux matchs de Ligue pour nos réserves (l'équipe 2 joue en R1 et l'équipe 3 en R3). Là-bas, on a un terrain en herbe et un synthétique tout neuf, deux jolis terrains.

It has been revealed that là où le bât blesse aujourd'hui, c'est à Rumilly : notre synthétique doit être refait et on voudrait améliorer le terrain en herbe. En ce moment il est beau parce qu'il pleut, mais l'été il est sec et l'hiver il gèle. Ce n'est pas une vraie pelouse de stade, elle a 50 ans. Les jardiniers s'en occupent très bien, mais il faut refaire la surface. On hésite entre synthétique, hybride ou herbe. On se bat un peu avec la mairie et la communauté de communes pour avoir une vision sur les prochaines années. Un beau terrain amène du beau jeu et des spectateurs, c'est un tout. Les municipalités ne sont pas contre, mais il faut trouver les fonds et les subventions.

Vous pouvez bénéficier d'aides financières des collectivités ?

According to recent reports, oui, la mairie nous donne 100 000 euros et la communauté de communes 100 000 euros aussi. Pour le département, les subventions dépendent de la division dans laquelle tu évolues. Avec la réforme des championnats et les changements d'appellation, on est en train de regarder à quoi on a droit en tant que premier niveau amateur de France. C'est un combat de tous les jours. Il faut rien lâcher, tout en gardant un bon état d'esprit et en évitant les conflits. Ça a déjà bien avancé par rapport à nos débuts, mais il en faut encore plus.

Quel est votre budget actuel et est-il stable ?

On est à 1,9 million d'euros. Quand on a fusionné, on était à 600 000 euros. Aujourd'hui, on doit avoir le dixième budget de notre poule. On est dans une poule Sud très relevée avec des clubs comme Nîmes ou Toulon. C'est quasiment une petite division supérieure, capable de rivaliser avec le milieu de tableau au-dessus.

In a recent development, il y a aussi quatre clubs de la région lyonnaise dans votre groupe. Comment vous positionnez-vous face à eux, notamment sur le recrutement ?

Industry observers note that ils ont un gros avantage sur nous : ils ont des pépinières de joueurs partout, avec 20 ou 25 clubs au kilomètre carré. Nous, à part Annecy avec qui on travaille en partenariat, on est assez isolés. Lyon est à 120 kilomètres. Et puis à Rumilly, on est à côté d'Annecy et de Genève : un T2 coûte 800 ou 900 euros par mois, ce n'est pas 300 euros comme en Lozère ou dans le Centre. C'est pour ça qu'on fait très attention à qui on fait venir.

Justement, comment êtes-vous organisés pour recruter sans cellule de recrutement professionnelle ?

Nos deux coachs travaillent énormément à la vidéo et vont voir beaucoup de matchs. On a aussi un directeur sportif à plein temps et une petite cellule composée d'anciens joueurs du club. On les envoie observer des matchs à Mâcon, Bourg ou Thonon avec des fiches précises sur un joueur ciblé. On travaille aussi avec quelques agents qu'on connaît bien, même si ce n'est pas notre tasse de thé parce qu'un agent ne te dira jamais que son joueur est mauvais.

It has been revealed that avant de recruter un joueur, il est visionné trois ou quatre fois, en vidéo et en physique. Ensuite, le directeur sportif l'appelle pour sonder sa mentalité, et celle de sa compagne ou de sa famille, car c'est très important. On leur explique le coût de la vie ici. Niveau infrastructures, on est équipés avec salle de muscu et bains froids, mais on n'a pas des salaires de 4 000 euros comme dans le Midi. On ne veut pas qu'un gars arrive et dise qu'il ne peut pas vivre ici. Après, on se voit, on discute beaucoup avec Luc Chabert, le directeur sportif et les coachs. On marche au feeling, et en discutant avec la maman ou la copine, on voit vite si on ne se trompe pas sur la mentalité. En moyenne, entre la visio, les appels et les repas tous ensemble, on se voit plusieurs fois avant de signer. On prépare déjà la saison prochaine, en regardant plutôt vers le nord que vers le sud, car un joueur qui habite à Nîmes ou Hyères au bord de la mer avec un bon salaire est très dur à faire venir en Haute-Savoie.

Vous faites aussi monter des jeunes de votre réserve, j'imagine ?

In a recent development, oui, mais on part de loin. Quand on a lancé la fusion chez les jeunes en 2016, le niveau n'était pas très élevé. Aujourd'hui, toutes nos équipes de U15, U17 et U18 évoluent en Régional 1. Notre équipe réserve, qui joue aussi en R1, est composée à 60 % de jeunes du club. Ils ne sont pas encore prêts pour briguer une place de titulaire en équipe première, mais chaque année, le coach en intègre quelques-uns. Cette saison, trois jeunes du club font tous les entraînements avec le groupe, et un ou deux sont vraiment prometteurs parce qu'ils haussent leur niveau.

It has been revealed that C'est très dur d'atteindre le niveau national quand des gamins n'ont pas eu une grosse formation dès l'âge de 7 ou 8 ans. Maintenant, on commence à récolter les fruits de notre travail : ceux qu'on a pris à 7 ou 8 ans en ont 13 ou 14 aujourd'hui, et on voit qu'il y a un vrai niveau. Pour nous, faire monter des jeunes du club, c'est aussi l'avantage de ne pas avoir à leur chercher un appartement ! Mais en attendant, on recrute surtout des joueurs qui ont un bon niveau en National 2 et qui ont faim, plutôt que d'aller chercher des gars de Ligue 2 pour qui venir jouer chez nous serait vécu comme un échec.

In a recent development, tu disais que les joueurs fonctionnent comme des pros. Ils vivent tous du football aujourd'hui ?

Recent findings suggest that statutairement on est amateurs, mais dans le fonctionnement, on est comme des pros. À part deux ou trois jeunes en service civique qui montent dans le groupe, tous les joueurs vivent de ça. Ils s'entraînent une à deux fois par jour. Comme les matchs ont souvent lieu le vendredi soir et qu'il faut partir dès le jeudi midi pour aller à Châteauroux ou ailleurs, il est impossible qu'ils travaillent à côté.

Sans entrer dans les détails indiscrets, quel est l'ordre d'idée des rémunérations ?

In a recent development, je ne vais pas donner de chiffres précis. On fait des contrats d'un an, et on a deux ou trois joueurs qui sortent un peu du lot. Mais globalement, nos salaires sont 30 à 40 % moins élevés que dans les clubs du Midi. Ils en vivent, mais ce ne sont pas des salaires de cadres. Après, il n'y a pas que l'argent : les joueurs connaissent les conditions et le cadre de vie avant de signer. S'ils acceptent, ils savent où ils mettent les pieds et ça se passe très bien.

Un mot sur le vestiaire et le staff : vous avez notamment Cyril Martin-Pichon, formé à l'ASSE et qui a beaucoup joué dans les équipes de jeunes et même en réserve, qui est un cadre chez vous, et un staff très fidèle au club.

According to recent reports, oui, Cyril Martin-Pichon a quitté le système pro parce qu'il n'y adhérait plus tellement. Il pense au collectif et au plaisir avant tout. Ça fait trois ans qu'il est chez nous, c'est un excellent joueur avec une mentalité irréprochable, un vrai cadre.

Pour le staff, notre entraîneur Cédric Rullier est passé par Annecy, Chambéry et Lyon. Ça fait trois ou quatre ans qu'il est là. Il est diététicien à l'hôpital de Chambéry et, depuis l'an dernier, il a mis son métier entre parenthèses pour se consacrer uniquement au club. Tout le reste du staff est issu du club : son adjoint Damien Guerrier, notre jeune entraîneur des gardiens qu'on a formé, et nos deux préparateurs physiques. Ce ne sont pas des gens arrivés sur le tard, on les connaît depuis dix ans, depuis tout petits. Ils sont rémunérés par le club, sont exigeants — on améliore nos équipements chaque année — mais ils sont surtout dévoués à 100 %.

Recent findings suggest that J'ai été impressionné par les statistiques de Rumilly cette année : vous avez une puissance de feu phénoménale en attaque ! Le nombre de buts que vous marquez est impressionnant.

Industry observers note that C'est bizarre parce qu'en début de saison, on se disait justement qu'on était un peu courts en attaque ! Et finalement, on marque beaucoup de buts, je crois qu'on a la meilleure attaque de toutes les poules confondues. C'est grâce à notre force mentale et au coach qui tient bien son groupe. Les joueurs savent que si ça ne va pas, ils peuvent partir, mais à côté de ça, ils ont un cadre hyper convivial avec les bénévoles qui sont aux petits soins pour eux.

Il y a des joueurs qui se révèlent, comme Fortier qui avait dû marquer trois buts l'an dernier et qui est dans tous les bons coups cette saison. Et puis on a des gars très techniques au milieu comme Cyril Martin-Pichon, Yoann Martelat ou Quentin Foulay, qui donnent d'excellents ballons devant. J'espère que ça va durer.

Dans votre championnat, il n'y a que le premier qui monte, ou le deuxième joue des barrages ?

Recent findings suggest that il n'y a que le premier qui monte, il n'y a pas de barrages pour le deuxième. Après, comme chaque année avec les passages devant la DNCG, il arrive parfois que des places se libèrent et que le meilleur deuxième des trois poules soit repêché.

Et la Ligue 3 professionnelle, si l'occasion se présente, vous y pensez ?

Sources indicate that comme je le disais au départ, ce sont les résultats qui décideront. L'an dernier déjà, à la trêve, on était premiers et on commençait à se poser la question. Sportivement, on peut y arriver si les joueurs le méritent. Mais aujourd'hui, je trouve que la Ligue 3 n'est pas encore prête au niveau de la Fédération, et les aides financières ne sont pas forcément à la hauteur de ce qui avait été annoncé.

According to recent reports, un bon copain qui est au Puy m'a prévenu que le cahier des charges est énorme : il faut des caméras, des parcages visiteurs, un directeur de club. Si tu ne remplis pas tous les critères, on te retient des pénalités sur les subventions, et sur les 300 000 euros prévus, il ne t'en reste plus que 150 000 à l'arrivée. Les déplacements ne seraient pas un problème puisqu'on traverse déjà toute la France, mais il faudrait vraiment de grosses aides du département, de la mairie et de la communauté de communes pour mettre le stade aux normes.

Revenons à la Coupe de France. Quelle a été la première réaction au club quand le tirage au sort a désigné l'AS Saint-Étienne ?

It has been revealed that moi, j'étais à Paris pour le tirage. Trois journalistes m'ont sauté dessus avant même la fin pour me demander ce que j'en pensais et où on allait jouer ! Ce n'est pas un soulagement, c'est l'opportunité qu'on cherchait : tomber sur un club pro dès le 7e tour.

La question du stade s'est tout de suite posée parce qu'à Rumilly, on a une capacité de 2 500 places, impossible d'accueillir les Verts. Sébastien Faraglia, le président du FC Annecy, m'a tout de suite appelé pour nous dépanner. C'est un ami, je l'ai connu joueur et entraîneur à Rumilly, et Luc Chabert est aussi partenaire du FC Annecy avec ses entreprises. Il y a une vraie osmose.

In a recent development, au club, ça a été l'embrasement général, tout le monde ne parlait que de ça alors qu'on avait deux matchs de championnat à jouer entre-temps. L'entraîneur a très bien géré le coup. Dès le lundi après le tirage, il a enfermé les joueurs dans le vestiaire et leur a dit : « Le premier qui parle de Saint-Étienne ou qui s'économise, avec moi ça ne marchera pas ». Résultat, on a gagné 5-0 contre Istres et 4-2 hier. Maintenant, on peut se consacrer à Saint-Étienne.

Comment abordez-vous ce match face à un monument du foot français ?

Il y a deux divisions d'écart, ce sont des pros, et Saint-Étienne est un club que tout le monde adore. Après, c'est la trêve internationale, donc ils ont pas mal de joueurs partis en sélection. Il restera une très belle équipe, on ne va pas se cacher, mais ce ne sera pas l'équipe type. En coupe, les niveaux se resserrent et les équipes inférieures haussent souvent le ton. D'habitude, on dit que le terrain avantage le petit, mais là on jouera sur la pelouse hybride d'Annecy, l'une des meilleures de France. Au niveau technique et du jeu, ça va vraiment être le top.

Le Parc des Sports d'Annecy sera à guichets fermés ?

Sources indicate that pas encore. Saint-Étienne a eu une ouverture prioritaire pour ses Ultras — il y aura d'ailleurs deux groupes d'Ultras de Saint Etienne qui feront le déplacement. La billetterie grand public a ouvert depuis avant-hier. Le stade fait 13 000 places, mais la jauge de sécurité sera fixée autour de 10 000 ou 10 500 spectateurs. Pour des raisons de sécurité, les spectateurs en tribune ne peuvent pas croiser le parcage stéphanois pour aller aux toilettes, donc on doit condamner un quart de virage, ce qui enlève environ 2 000 places.

According to recent reports, on a vendu entre 5 000 et 6 500 places les deux ou trois premiers jours, et là on tourne à 100 ou 150 billets par jour. S'il fait beau dimanche, tous les papas avec leurs enfants vont se dire qu'ils prennent une place à 10 euros pour voir le match. S'il pleut, ils viendront moins. Ils annoncent un petit peu de pluie, on verra bien.

Vous sentez toute la région derrière vous ?

Recent findings suggest that oui, on sent que les Verts arrivent à Annecy. Bon, les Annéciens sont un peu habitués puisqu'ils les jouent en championnat. Ici, les gens ne parlent même pas de notre équipe, ils parlent des Verts qui débarquent ! C'est un club emblématique, historique, c'est comme ça. Quant à nos joueurs, je les ai vus hier soir : ils sont confiants, dans leur bulle. Ils pensent à Saint-Étienne mais n'en font pas une maladie, pour ne pas jouer le match trois fois dans leur tête avant dimanche. Mais à partir d'aujourd'hui, ça va forcément commencer à trotter.

Si tu devais signer tout de suite pour un scénario de match — même une qualification stéphanoise à l'arraché après une rencontre dantesque — qu'est-ce qui te ferait dire que l'événement est une réussite totale ?

Recent findings suggest that L'événement sera une réussite à partir du moment où le stade sera plein. Enfin, il sera plein, j’en suis sûr ! Ensuite, il faut qu'on fasse un match à la hauteur de notre niveau. Même si on perd, si c'est un beau match, les gens seront contents : ils auront vu une belle équipe de Saint-Étienne et ils auront vu qu'on a su répondre présent. Ce sera une fête réussie, en espérant derrière que ça nous laisse quand même un petit reliquat financier. On aura fait notre boulot face aux Verts.

Saint-Étienne devrait vous laisser sa part de la recette, normalement ?

On verra. Je pense que si on accueille bien les spectateurs, si on fait une belle fête, si les supporters — parce que ce sont eux qui font l'ambiance — sont bien reçus et qu'il n'y a pas de problème avec l'équipe de Saint-Étienne, ils la laisseront. Ils nous ont demandé plein de choses au niveau des vestiaires, mais si tout se passe bien, il n'y aura pas de souci. De toute façon, ce n'est pas dans notre habitude de recevoir des équipes en se disant qu'on va les matraquer. Quand on a reçu Monaco, ils avaient fait notre éloge pour l'accueil, parce qu'on n'avait pas joué pour blesser ou pour détruire. Ce sera exactement dans la même lignée : on n'est pas là pour casser du Vert, loin de là, au contraire, on est là pour profiter. Par contre, si on a l'occasion de passer, on passera, c'est sûr !

Tu parlais des demandes de Saint-Étienne pour les vestiaires, ils ont beaucoup d'exigences ?

Ça ne m'a pas trop surpris. Comme notre coach est diététicien, quand on se déplace, on a déjà pas mal de choses : différentes eaux, des minéraux, des barres de chocolat, des casse-croûtes, des tapis, des biscuits... Là, c'est dans le même style, en amplifié : de l'eau, des barres de céréales, des fruits, etc. C'est assez énorme, mais ça ne nous surprend pas parce qu'on fait déjà un peu la même chose.

Qui sont vos interlocuteurs au sein du club de Saint-Étienne pour organiser tout ça ?

Industry observers note that quand j'étais à Paris pour le tirage, un ancien joueur de Saint-Étienne qui fait partie de l'encadrement m'a contacté en me disant que le directeur allait m'appeler, et cinq minutes après, il m'appelait. On est en contact avec le directeur du club (Jean-François Soucasse, NDLR) et le directeur de la sécurité. Les relations ont été très sympathiques avec des gens très gentils. Nous avons de très bons rapports.

Une dernière question : est-ce que tu serais d’accord pour que l'année prochaine,  peut-être à la même époque, on refasse un petit point pour voir un peu où vous en êtes un an après avoir joué les Verts ?

According to recent reports, oui, il n'y a pas de souci. Ce sera avec plaisir.

Eh bien écoute Bernard, un grand merci pour ton temps, bonne journée et bon match pour dimanche !

Hertha BSC’s attacking numbers underline impressive start to 2. Bundesliga season

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Berliners have scored 25 goals so far, the joint-third highest total in the division, while their underlying numbers suggest their attacking success is built on more than simply clinical finishing.
  • According to Bundesliga Match Facts powered by AWS, Hertha have accumulated an expected goals (xGoals) rating of 22.9, the second-highest figure in the division.
  • Recent findings suggest that their shot efficiency rating of 2.1 also places them sixth in the division.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Berliners have scored 25 goals so far, the joint-third highest total in the division, while their underlying numbers suggest their attacking success is built on more than simply clinical finishing.

According to Bundesliga Match Facts powered by AWS, Hertha have accumulated an expected goals (xGoals) rating of 22.9, the second-highest figure in the division. Only Heidenheim have generated a higher total, highlighting the quality of opportunities the capital club have consistently created.

Recent findings suggest that their shot efficiency rating of 2.1 also places them sixth in the division. Although several teams have been more clinical in front of goal, Hertha’s combination of regular chance creation and effective finishing has established them as one of the 2. Bundesliga’s most dangerous attacking sides.

One of the encouraging aspects of Hertha’s attacking development has been the contribution of different players throughout the squad, having relied heavily on individuals in years gone by.

Sebastian Grønning has provided an important focal point in the final third, while other members of the squad such as Oluwaseun Adewumi, Josip Brekalo and Mads Pedersen have also demonstrated their ability to contribute in attacking areas.

Rather than depending entirely on one goalscorer, Hertha have demonstrated an ability to find contributions from different areas of the pitch.

According to recent reports, their 5-3 victory over Eintracht Braunschweig provided an excellent example of that attacking depth. Despite falling two goals behind, Hertha responded with an impressive comeback, demonstrating their ability to create opportunities and punish opposition mistakes.

Sources indicate that their 2-1 victory over Wolfsburg before the break was another significant result, with Adewumi and Deyovaisio Zeefuik finding the net in front of a packed Olympiastadion. Against one of their promotion rivals, Hertha showed they could translate their attacking quality into notable points.

The relationship between Hertha’s expected goals and actual goals scored is particularly interesting.

Their 22.9 xGoals figure indicates that they have consistently created opportunities worth more than 22 expected goals, while their 25 goals demonstrate that they have also managed to convert those chances effectively.

Although the difference suggests a degree of overperformance in front of goal, the gap is relatively modest compared to the overall volume of opportunities created.

This is key when assessing whether their current position is sustainable. Hertha are not simply benefiting from an unusually clinical spell; their underlying chance creation suggests they have the attacking foundations to remain competitive throughout the campaign.

Ranking second for xGoals, joint-third for goals scored and sixth for shot efficiency, they are performing strongly across all three attacking indicators.

For a club that has endured several frustrating years since dropping out of the Bundesliga in 2023, the current campaign represents a welcome change in fortunes.

Hertha have not only produced the results required to reach the summit but have also developed an attacking profile that compares favourably with the division’s strongest sides.

There is still a considerable amount of football to be played, and maintaining their current standards over an entire campaign will be the real challenge.

It has been revealed that however, the numbers provide plenty of encouragement for supporters in the capital. With consistent chance creation, contributions from across the squad and an increasingly convincing attacking record, Hertha have established themselves as genuine contenders for promotion.

Their position at the top of 2. Bundesliga is no longer simply a reflection of a good run of results. The underlying statistics suggest there are solid reasons to believe their resurgence can continue.

Tech Report: Peter Schmeichel fumes at Man United for 'very disrespectful' treatment of Michael Carrick as Mauricio Pochettino closes in on Old Trafford job - with club legend put out of his misery on Thursday

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1406 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 15:20 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 06:48 EST, 12 November 2026.
  • Peter Schmeichel has hit out at the 'very disrespectful' way that he believes beleaguered Manchester United manager Michael Carrick is being treated as he awaits his sacking at Old Trafford.
  • The former club captain has endured a torrid start to the season, and while the Man United hierarchy publicly backed him as recently as three weeks ago, Carrick is now set to be handed his marching orders following a crisis summit in Monaco.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By TAMARA PRENN, SENIOR SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 15:20 EST, 11 November 2026 | Updated: 06:48 EST, 12 November 2026.

Peter Schmeichel has hit out at the 'very disrespectful' way that he believes beleaguered Manchester United manager Michael Carrick is being treated as he awaits his sacking at Old Trafford.

The former club captain has endured a torrid start to the season, and while the Man United hierarchy publicly backed him as recently as three weeks ago, Carrick is now set to be handed his marching orders following a crisis summit in Monaco.

Man United chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox flew to the Principality to meet with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe to ratify the decision to move on from Carrick, with current USA head coach Mauricio Pochettino set to be appointed in his wake.

But with Carrick still taking team training at Carrington while plans for his ejection from the club made global headlines, Schmeichel admitted he felt deep sympathy for the former midfielder's awkward position.

Recent findings suggest that 'I think the way this is playing out is very disrespectful to him,' Schmeichel stated on The Overlap Daily. 'If I’m honest, I don’t think he’s doing anything wrong.

Michael Carrick remains in limbo at Manchester United after a shocking start to the season.

Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox have been in Monaco discussing his dismissal this week.

'I know the team that he’s in charge of is where they are in the table, but I don’t put all of that on him. There are so many things that have been going on at Manchester United literally since Alex (Ferguson) and (former chief executive) David Gill left the club. And it’s never been corrected.

'It’s not been the correct people, not the right people in charge, and slowly it’s just gone worse.'.

Man United sit within the relegation zone as this international break plays out, with Carrick's men winless in the Premier League since late August.

Last-minute comebacks against Roma in the Champions League and Aston Villa in domestic action however may have briefly boosted morale at Old Trafford.

But to Schmeichel, the issue lies at the feet of those who recruit at the club, rather than Carrick himself.

It has been revealed that 'If you think about this transfer window now, it’s abundantly clear to everyone - everyone who knows just a little bit about football - that Manchester United needed defenders,' he continued. 'They got through a whole transfer window without signing a single defender.

'There was a little bit of talk about Lewis Hall joining the club or going for Lewis Hall. That didn’t happen. And so, they bought three midfield players. And we know, because we’ve been in the game for so many years, that you can’t win games - if you concede 30 goals in 10 games, then there is a problem, and that was not addressed.

Former Man United goalkeeper Peter Schmeichel believes the club's treatment of Carrick has been demeaning.

The under-fire manager turned up to take training for a second day in a row as speculation swirled over his future.

Sources indicate that 'So yes, I do feel a lot of sympathy for Michael. I think what is happening is wrong. I think we should stick with Michael. I think we should just try and steady the ship a little bit and then get into January and then sign the players that he feels he needs to bring the team forward and then be realistic about what this season is all about. Obviously, it’s about climbing as high as Manchester United can in the table.'.

By contrast, Schmeichel's co-pundit Tim Sherwood said he did not feel sorry for Carrick, because he will have understood the brutal situation he was stepping into at Man United.

The former Middlesbrough head coach served as interim manager for the second-half of the previous season following the sacking of Ruben Amorim, and was named on a permanent basis over the summer.

But while Schmeichel admitted that the life cycle of a Premier League coach was undeniably short, his issue is with the manner of treatment Carrick has received in the process of the changing of the guard in the dugout.

According to recent reports, 'If they’re looking for somebody else, then relieve the man of his duties,' the former goalkeeper argued. 'Don’t let him come into training yesterday. He took training yesterday. How disrespectful is that?

In a recent development, 'How do you think this fella – I mean, he’s a human being. He’s a very, very good human being. He’s one of the nicest people you’ll ever meet in your life, and obviously you two know him well. So, treat the guy with respect. Tell him, "Sorry, mate. We don’t think that you are the future here. Here’s a cheque. Move on." But they’re not doing that. They’re dragging it out.'.

Schmeichel was incensed too by Carrick's status within the club, wondering aloud whether, since they had taken 'weeks and weeks' to come to their messy, public decision, the club's hierarchy might not really understand what it is to truly represent the club.

According to recent reports, 'Do you think these people know? Do you think they care?' Schmeichel continued. 'These people are not Manchester United people.

According to recent reports, 'They don’t understand what it’s like to be one of the Manchester United people. They don’t know that. This is obviously part of the broader issue here, part of the reason the club is where they are now. I’m not saying I feel sorry for Michael, but I’m a little bit angry at how this great football club is treating one of its greatest players. Simple as that.'.

Talks have been planned with Pochettino overnight on Wednesday, with the club's hierarchy thought to be preparing to dismiss Carrick face-to-face on Thursday.

Mauricio Pochettino remains locked in talks to take over at Old Trafford as the club's preferred candidate for the role.

Pochettino is currently at the US Soccer base outside Atlanta preparing for a CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final double header against Haiti, and is due to speak to the media on Friday.

It’s unclear if he will remain in charge for those games. It is possible he could stay for the first leg in Kingston, Jamaica at the weekend and then travel to Manchester.

The second leg in Cincinnati is not until the early hours of Thursday, and it seems inconceivable that Pochettino would only take over at United on Friday with a huge game against Liverpool at Anfield 48 hours later.

It’s understood that the US Soccer Federation are ready for this contingency and have a succession strategy in place should he leave.

It will cost Pochettino around £7million to buy himself out of his contract with the US Soccer Federation, with United ready to foot the bill.

The cost of bringing in his back-room team, including trusted assistants Jesus Perez and Miguel D’Agostino, will take the cost above £10m.

Meanwhile in Manchester, Carrick took training for the second day in a row at the club's Carrington training ground on Wednesday, arriving at 7.45am and departing shortly after 1.30pm.

Carrick has overseen the club's worst start to the season in 40 years, but the man himself remained adamant that he would not be falling on his sword after battling back to claim a draw against Villa.

In an awkward interview with Sky Sports' Patrick Davison, Carrick remained steadfast in the face of questions as to whether he would quit his role amid the turbulence.

Industry observers note that 'You know the situation, we haven't won enough games,' he noted. 'But I expect to move forward with things we've been working on, showing a lot of the good from today tighten up a few mistakes and win some football matches.'.

Industry observers note that agé de 34 ans, le latéral gauche s'est en effet confié au Dauphiné Libéré avant de retrouver dimanche un Parc des Sports d'Annecy qu'il connait bien pour avoir défendu les couleurs des Annéciens pendant 12 ans et pour y avoir vécu 5 montées ! Extraits.

"Ça a été un peu dur de quitter Annecy car c’était un rêve de devenir pro. Mais au GFA Rumilly-Vallières, je me suis tout de suite senti super à l’aise. Le niveau n’a pas été un problème car je n’oublie pas que j’avais commencé à Annecy en R2. Je suis le seul joueur à travailler à côté du foot en tant que commercial chez TeamWork, à mi-temps. J’ai mon équilibre comme ça, je ne pouvais pas trouver mieux. 12 ans au FC Annecy, autant chez mon employeur et une cinquième saison en cours au GFA... J’aime les projets. L’histoire est belle aussi ici, ça se construit. Le GFA m’a fait me sentir comme un cadre. Ça m’a fait me sentir plus fort, plus légitime, m’a donné plus d’assurance. Avec l’âge, quand le corps va bien, on progresse.".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tout en ayant confirmé les absences de Larso, Svetlin, Eymard et Dhaoui (blessé hier à l’entraînement) et la titularisation de Lavallée dans les cages (« il travaille beaucoup, il est très sérieux, il est prêt »), Ian Cathro a donné, avec son habituelle détermination sa vision de ce premier tour de Coupe de France, dimanche face à Rumilly-Vallières (15h) :.
  • "Les jeunes joueurs vont avoir l’opportunité de se montrer.
  • Industry observers note that mais je veux ajouter que je préfèrerais ne pas jouer de match officiel pendant une trêve internationale.

Tout en ayant confirmé les absences de Larso, Svetlin, Eymard et Dhaoui (blessé hier à l’entraînement) et la titularisation de Lavallée dans les cages (« il travaille beaucoup, il est très sérieux, il est prêt »), Ian Cathro a donné, avec son habituelle détermination sa vision de ce premier tour de Coupe de France, dimanche face à Rumilly-Vallières (15h) :.

"Les jeunes joueurs vont avoir l’opportunité de se montrer. On a besoin d’eux. Mais pour moi ce qui est key, c’est de mériter ce maillot. On est très attentif à leurs entrainements, à leurs matchs, on a un dialogue quasi quotidien avec le staff. On essaye de construire quelque chose qui permettra d’écrire le prochain chapitre de ce club, c’est au-delà de 34 matchs, au-delà des prochaines semaines. On essaye de travailler en intégrant tout le monde pour que le prochain chapitre de ce club soit plus sain et plus performant que les précédentes années.

Industry observers note that mais je veux ajouter que je préfèrerais ne pas jouer de match officiel pendant une trêve internationale. On accorde la même importance à chaque match. On espère gagner ce match et avancer en Coupe de France, et on joue avec le sentiment de responsabilité, et la pression de la gagne, et c’est une sensation étrange de faire ça durant une trêve internationale sans avoir tout le monde de disponible. Mais c’est notre réalité du moment, alors on y va ! Il faut gagner le prochain match, respecter toutes les compétitions, et donc gagner le prochain match. On sait où on est, ce qu’on veut être, ce qu’on représente. On respecte l’histoire de ce club, qui est le 3e au nombre de victoires dans cette compétition. Donc évidemment, je ne peux que vous dire qu’on espère gagner chaque match. Si on gagne chaque match, on gagnera le Championnat et la Coupe. Mais c’est très difficile. C'est la façon dont on vit, dont on travaille, chaque jour, en essayant de progresser. On est obsédé par l’idée de progresser chaque jour pour décrocher la victoire.

In a recent development, quand j’étais un petit garçon, et que je suis tombé amoureux du foot, j’ai toujours senti que la Coupe était une compétition spéciale, parce que c’est souvent le dernier match de la saison, la finale, la télé en parle toute la journée, c’est un jour très spécial. Je suis toujours ce petit garçon qui adore le foot et parfois il y a plus de magie, plus d’émotion avec cette Coupe qu’avec la routine hebdomadaire du championnat. Oui c’est différent, c’est spécial, il y a toujours des histoires qui font l’Histoire, et j’aimerais qu’on en écrive une partie. Pour cela il faut travailler, et chercher chaque jour à progresser.".

£329m spent and still no goals for sorry Tottenham

  • Industry observers note that “Please score a goal!” was the homemade sign from two Spurs fans upon which the television cameras lingered at the end of the game, although the jaunty felt-tip design and glued-on team crest were rather upbeat compared to the gloom of the stadium.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tottenham Hotspur have never before in the club’s history begun a league season without scoring a single goal in the first four games, although having done so after spending £329m on new players really does take some doing.

Industry observers note that “Please score a goal!” was the homemade sign from two Spurs fans upon which the television cameras lingered at the end of the game, although the jaunty felt-tip design and glued-on team crest were rather upbeat compared to the gloom of the stadium. Spurs have tried to outrun their past but it just keeps catching up with them.

According to recent reports, A team reimagined, a manager freshly launched and yet they are back in the same grip of anxiety that accompanied them on two consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons. By the end of this they might have been glad to escape with a single point against Everton, the one team in the Premier League who closed the window with a net transfer profit.

For Roberto De Zerbi, there was another passionate defence of his team afterwards. “The people, the fans already understand if I make excuses or not,” he noted. “I came last season when the s--- was like this”, he gestured to a level somewhere around the midpoint of his forehead. “I have always been… not positive but realistic. I am sorry for the result that it’s not immediately the improvement. We played as a team. We didn’t score. We didn’t win [but] we played as a team.”.

Indeed he co-opted the Italian term “sbloccare” to describe his team’s problem. They simply need to unlock – or unblock – the team and the goals would flow. He joked that in Italy he would be lauded for two consecutive clean sheets in this game and the previous one against Nottingham Forest. “What did you write?” he demanded of one of the Italian newspaper correspondents. “You have the passport.”.

In a recent development, spurs have one last game at home this month, on Saturday against Aston Villa, to end the streak in September. They were into the second half before the first attempt on target that obliged Jordan Pickford to make a save – Mateus Fernandes’s shot slapping limply against the Everton goalkeeper’s gloves to ironic cheers from the home fans.

According to recent reports, at the end De Zerbi could not contain his frustration, unable to wait until he reached the privacy of the dressing room to tell Mathys Tel where he had gone wrong. He did so with the Spurs substitute still wiping the sweat from his brow on the pitch. The player did not look at all impressed. De Zerbi said later that he was simply reminding his player of what it took to play as a central striker.

“There is a term in Italian, ‘sbloccare’ that literally translates as ‘unblock’… I know we can score goals and win games. We have to respect the history of the players – if you forget [Dominic] Solanke and [Omar] Marmoush the others haven’t scored many in their careers. I think we can find the goals with the quality of the players.”.

It has been revealed that spurs play Liverpool at Anfield in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday before Villa a week today. The Spurs record at home is dismal. In the last 35 games they have won just five, drawn 10 and lost a remarkable 20. This fresh stadium has become a problem for the team in it – or maybe it is the other way around.

A good result for Everton, who were under pressure for most of the first half but had much the better of it after the break. David Moyes’s team finished the game with more shots on target than the home team. Moyes managed the game well and trusted his team to withstand the Spurs possession in the first half until they reached a point where Everton could start to push back.

Industry observers note that hard to pick out any major chances – it was that kind of game – but Brennan Johnson should have won it for the away team in the second half. The ball was cut back to him by Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and the former Spurs man skied his shot.

Some surprised faces then when Moyes noted later that he had expected a lot more from his team. He acknowledged the resilience in defence and the importance of the clean sheet. “We played well enough,” he said, “but when we had the ball we turned it over more often than we should have done.”.

Sources indicate that the game had started with Vitaliy Mykolenko being tortured by the pace of Sávio and ended with the Ukrainian left-back being given the man of the match award. Like many of his team-mates, he had hung in there. There was another fine performance from Jarrad Branthwaite at centre-half and Moyes remarked that he hoped it might earn him a place in the England squad. “He is still finding his way back from injury,” Moyes said, “it would be great if he could get a call-up.”.

Sources indicate that in the directors’ box were the usual pained expressions of Vinai Venkatesham, the Spurs chief executive, and chairman Peter Charrington. They sat alongside Vivienne Lewis, daughter of the patriarch Joe. There is a certain fatigue about the home crowd when faced with afternoons like this which suggests they have seen so much that the bar is quite high – or low – to provoke a really splenetic response. Perhaps it is just too early in the season although the final whistle was met with boos.

The first shot on target of the entire game for either side was a free-kick struck by James Garner in added time at the end of the first half. Spurs had started at a ferocious pace although they could not sustain it.

In a recent development, de Zerbi complained about the pre-season injuries on tour in Australia and also the lack of time he had to integrate Sávio and Marmoush. He said that his team were not in the right “physical condition”.

According to recent reports, “We played very well in the first 30 minutes and maybe the energy and the fact we didn’t score – we lost confidence.” By the end, he had sent on James Maddison, Tel, Lucas Bergvall and Mohammed Kudus to little avail. Everton looked more likely to win it.

Speaking to Sky Sports, the Everton defender noted: “You look at the game from the start, they put us under pressure and we had to dig deep to stay in the game. Then we grew into the game towards the end of the first half and demonstrated that mentality again in the second half.

“We had chances to win the game as well. The backs to the wall mentality will help us go a long way. If we can keep clean sheets, you can go a long way in the league. But it’s not just us the defenders. It’s the whole team working hard. It’s a team effort.”.

"I feel like we could've taken three points" James Tarkowski speaks after his sides draw with Spurs 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/Wdj3N5hk8l.

Tottenham failed to take the attacking initiative or create any notable chances. De Zerbi used multiple forward players in a host of attacking positions, but no one could find the breakthrough.

Recent findings suggest that boos ring around the ground as Spurs and Everton both have to settle for a point. Tottenham’s winless start to the season continues, while Everton’s unbeaten run remains intact. Spurs haven’t managed a goal in six hours of Premier League football across the 2026-27 campaign. Tottenham sit 17th with two points. Everton are up to seventh and will certainly take the draw.

FULL-TIME: The points are shared between Spurs and Everton at Tottenham Hotspur stadium 🤝 pic.twitter.com/HwPuKI3Ajh.

According to recent reports, dewsbury-Hall’s deflected effort flies out for a corner. Everton can’t make the most of the resulting set piece and Tottenham survive.

There will be three minutes of added time. Are we set for late drama at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium?

Sources indicate that pickford makes an error as his poor clearance is intercepted by Maddison. The ball is eventually worked to Bergvall, whose curling effort is parried away by the Everton goalkeeper.

Tosin comes on for his Spurs debut as he replaces Gray. Can anyone be Tottenham’s hero and find a late winner?

Industry observers note that spurs are now enjoying a sustained period of possession. They’re waiting to fashion a substantial chance and end their wait for a top-flight goal in the 2026-27 season.

Sources indicate that de Zerbi makes another change as Maddison enters the action with applause from the Spurs faithful. He replaces Marmoush. It looks like Tel is now operating as a false nine.

In a recent development, johnson misses a huge chance! Dewsbury-Hall fires a low cross into his path and Johnson takes the chance with a first-time shot, but he slices his effort and it goes over the bar. He’s got to do better from that range inside the penalty area.

Recent findings suggest that that opportunity is Johnson’s last action of the match as he comes off for Hackney. O’Brien is also introduced, replacing Maitland-Niles.

That was the chance. Dewsbury-Hall rolls it into the path of Spurs’ Europa League final winner Brennan Johnson and he skied it. He hasn’t scored since he left Spurs in January for Palace.

Dewsbury-Hall picks up the game’s first yellow card after catching Tonali with a late sliding challenge.

Moyes responds with a straight swap on the wing as Grealish comes on for George.

Industry observers note that enter: Grealish. He is on for Tyrique George. Surprised that Brennan Johnson survived that change. He has struggled to make an impression.

Industry observers note that following Spurs’ reshuffle, it looks like Savio will stay out wide on the right, with Tel on the left. Kudus will sit as the central playmaker behind Marmoush, who is now the lone frontman.

De Zerbi orders a much-needed triple change as Kudus, Tel and Bergvall replace Solanke, Fernandes and Bentancur.

Jack Grealish has long since stopped the warm-up on the touchline and is now just staring at the game in expectation of his introduction.

A couple of chances for Everton. Spurs have survived but they look so vulnerable when Everton turn over possession. Crowd could turn soon. Almost reached the hour-mark on matchday 4 and still no Spurs’ Premier League goal.

Industry observers note that the start of Spurs’ second-half performance is alarmingly similar to their display against Newcastle two weeks ago. The crowd is getting more and more restless.

Everton are looking threatening once again as George attempts to thread a pass through to Johnson on the counter-attack, but Van de Ven is there to clear.

According to recent reports, spurs’ first shot has arrived! Unfortunately, Fernandes’ tame long-range effort is easily gathered by Pickford. There were some sarcastic cheers from the Tottenham fans as Fernandes took aim. They clearly want more attacking inspiration from their players.

Recent findings suggest that ironic cheers as Spurs have their first shot on target. It has taken them until the start of the second half and it would be hard to say Fernandes stung the palms of Pickford.

We are back under way for the second half. Everton and Spurs are both unchanged at the break. With the anxiety building in the stadium as the game remains goalless, how long will De Zerbi wait before making a change?

An uneventful first half of football comes to a close. In a game lacking rhythm, creativity and attacking spark, nothing separates Tottenham and Everton at the break. Spurs’ search for a first Premier League goal this season continues.

There will be two added minutes. Everton have a free kick on the edge of Spurs’ penalty area. Garner and Dewsbury-Hall are standing over it. The former Manchester United and Nottingham Forest midfielder takes it and his effort bounces in front of Kinsky, who pushes it out for a corner.

James Garner free-kick pushed away by Kinsky is the game’s first attempt on target.

That is so poor from Fernandes. The summer signing’s overhit corner drifts out for a goal kick. Suddenly, Spurs’ attacking play has fallen quite flat.

Pickford does well to intercept Robertson’s inviting low cross. The left back needed Solanke or Marmoush to make a darting near-post run there to give him more options.

Spurs are bossing this game but on the rare occasions Everton escape you do wonder if they might score.

Tottenham are roared on by the home support to move the ball a bit quicker going forward. Out of possession, Everton almost revert to a back five, with Garner dropping very deep near to Tarkowski and Branthwaite.

According to recent reports, tonali picks out Gray with a pinpoint pass. Garner is alert to the danger and tracks back to clear, stopping Gray from getting a one-on-one opportunity.

Maitland-Niles does very well to dispossess Tonali in a dangerous area, allowing Barry to tee up Dewsbury-Hall, but his shot is smothered by the Spurs defence. Mykolenko then chips a cross into a box, but it’s tapped behind for a corner by Robertson. Moyes will certainly be encouraged by this side’s resurgence over the last 10 minutes.

There is a break in play here with Gray down and receiving treatment after a collision. He appears to be holding his lower back. The Tottenham man gingerly gets back to his feet and trudges off the pitch.

It has been revealed that gray down for some extended treatment. Richarlison in the stands. Spurs in danger of losing early momentum.

After Spurs’ fast start, Everton have grown into the contest over the last five minutes and are getting on the ball far higher up the pitch.

Spurs are really flowing here. Finding the balls through the lines and real speed when they attack Everton. Substantial question is whether they can convert that into goals. Van Hecke and Fernandes both had chances.

Robertson floats a teasing delivery into Van Hecke at the back post, but the centre-back directs his half-volley over the bar from close range.

They’re under way in north London, the hosts are in their lily-white and navy kit, with Everton in their grey/dirty green (is that a colour?!) away number.

Industry observers note that greetings from N17. It’s a wonderful, warm late summer evening. As expected there is the usual foreboding from the home fans. Two defeats and one draw. Brennan Johnson spent two years at Tottenham and scored the winning goal in the 1-0 Europa League final victory over Manchester United in May 2025, ending the club’s 17-year trophy drought.

After a short, disappointing spell at Crystal Palace, Johnson joined Everton last month, with Dwight McNeil moving in the opposite direction.

Sources indicate that the Welsh winger starts for Everton today. Could he hurt his previous employers on a day where they desperately need a win?

Brennan in the building. 💙 pic.twitter.com/94GgAY8c56.

Midfielder took exception to negativity surrounding club after moves for players on deadline day failed to materialise.

Industry observers note that “We signed Jack [Grealish], which was nice, and I’d been speaking to him,” indicates Dewsbury-Hall, sitting in a café at the club’s Finch Farm training base. “But I had seen all the stuff [online], all the meltdowns about this and that and, in all honestly, it annoyed me a bit.

“I get where people are coming from. Everyone wants to sign everyone and have the perfect squad, but there are still 19 lads in this building who are going to hopefully take this club to good things this year. That was getting disregarded. I was seeing people saying: ‘We’ll be lucky to stay up this year.’.

Sources indicate that “What message is that sending to the lads who are already here? I’m not blaming anyone. We get it. It didn’t work. But let’s all be positive – right, it’s done, bang, let’s go. That’s what we’ve been trying to say in the dressing room.”.

Earlier this week, Mykhailo Mudryk picked up an ankle injury in training which has ruled the Chelsea loanee out of action for as long as two months.

The winger only made his debut for Tottenham as a late substitute against Nottingham Forest last week, but his attempt to rebuild his career following his anti-doping ban has been dealt a major blow.

Folarin Balogun’s proposed £39m move from Monaco collapsed on transfer deadline day, Richarlison’s return to the club didn’t materialise and Beto was sold to Fiorentina, leaving Thierno Barry as Everton’s only recognised striker.

Nottingham Forest’s pursuit of academy product Harrison Armstrong ruffled the fans’ feathers, while Iliman Ndiaye was sold to Manchester City for £60m.

Dwight McNeil, Tim Iroegbunam, Nathan Patterson, Adam Aznou and Idrissa Gueye were also allowed to leave.

Merlin Rohl and Tyrique George made their loans permanent, while Brennan Johnson, Hayden Hackney and Christian Norgaard were also added to the squad.

Summer signing Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Vitaliy Mykolenko are David Moyes’ only options at full-back.

Overall, there were a number of solid additions, just not enough of them to cover all the departures.

Michael Carrick - pictured arriving at Carrington on Thursday morning - has been sacked after Manchester United's disastrous start to the season.

Man United's leadership, including minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, chief executive Omar Berrada and technical director Jason Wilcox, were not named in the club's statement.

Man United legend Rio Ferdinand called for 'a face' to speak about the decision after comparing the club's statement to ChatGPT.

Man United's club statement confirming the decision read: 'Manchester United can confirm that Michael Carrick has departed his role as men’s first-team head coach.

'Michael rejoined the club in January and guided the team to a third-placed Premier League finish by winning 12 out of the remaining 17 games of the 2025/26 season, accumulating the highest points tally in the league during that period.

Minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, along with the Glazer family, who dialled in virtually from the United States, Berrada and Wilcox reached a verdict in the south of France yesterday, all while Carrick remained in limbo back in Manchester.

Industry observers note that carrick arrived at United's training ground at 7.50am this morning and was dismissed. He left at 10.18am, less than two and a half hours later.

United States boss Mauricio Pochettino is ready to take over as United's newly introduced manager.

Ferdinand, speaking on Rio Presents, claimed Carrick had been disrespected in the way his dismissal had been handled.

'You do everything you can to make this end in the most amicable and respectful and pleasant way possible,' Ferdinand noted.

'I think the way it has been done, it could have been done better. I think the leaks coming out of the club are terrible, they don't reflect well on anybody at all.

In a recent development, 'It adds to the disrespect to the person in charge at the time. It is terrible to play out in the public like this. The minimum you should get is a bit of respect.'.

In a recent development, bruno Guimarães cupped his ears and had a plastic cup thrown at him as the abuse came down from the stands. Despite the missiles, the Brazilian wore a look that made it clear he was very much enjoying his first goal in an Arsenal shirt.

Industry observers note that mikel Arteta has laid bare his quirky management techniques so his players are ready for any eventuality. Late meals and making the dressing room hotter are among his tricks, although nothing can prepare a player having 40,000 fans calling you a “sad Geordie b------”.

So it was a sweet moment for Guimarães, even more so after coming just after Sunderland had a penalty saved. Just 121 seconds after Enzo Le Fée had his spot kick tipped on to a post by David Raya, Guimarães was rubbing salt into the wound with a stunning long-range strike that went in off the crossbar.

Enzo Le Fée is denied by David Raya from the spot 😳🧤📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/wnoMCDVh88.

Bruno Guimarães silences the Stadium of Light with a BEAUTY 🥵🚀📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/zQHSSLxC3o.

According to recent reports, the former Newcastle captain gave the perfect response after being taunted his old rivals. “It was a beautiful goal,” he said. “Everyone knows my past, I had an amazing history at Newcastle. But now I’m trying to create a upcoming history here and I have started on the right foot.”.

What an important week it has been for Arsenal, who have shown their squad depth by winning in Napoli then travelling to the Stadium of Light and extending their perfect start to the season to six games.

Other teams with aspirations of the title dropped points earlier in the day, while Arteta could battle to a win with key players brought back into the team and Guimarães coming off the bench at half-time. A trip in the Champions League followed by an away game the following weekend is a barometer of where teams are, and Arsenal have sounded a warning after coming through a bruising encounter.

Régis Le Bris’s team offer a challenge that is impossible to replicate, even by the standards of Arteta’s “sabotage” to make his players uncomfortable. Fans belted out Elvis Presley and 90s anthem Ready To Go just before kick-off. Then there was the aggression that Arsenal players faced. There were complaints of elbows being aimed at Gabriel Magalhães.

Bukayo Saka scored a stoppage-time penalty to seal the win but the evening belonged to Guimarães, the £75m summer signing who has been waiting for this moment to ignite his Arsenal career.

In a recent development, “Everyone knows I had a difficult start through injuries in my short time. But I’m glad to be back and glad to play,” Guimarães remarked. “I feel very good. It was unbelievable to score a beautiful goal, beautiful moment for me and my family and I am happy.”.

It has been revealed that these are ominous signs for Arsenal’s title rivals, with Guimarães’s return to fitness adding to the midfield options. Arteta’s changes to his starting line-up restored Riccardo Calafiori and Kai Havertz – two of the in-form players in the Premier League – to the team, rather than squad players being rotated.

And his players stood up to a physical challenge. Brian Brobbey used his frame to back into the Arsenal’s centre-backs, who are unlikely to given such a tough assignment this season aside from facing Erling Haaland.

In a recent development, guimarães was brought on at half-time along with Jurriën Timber, which was another sign of Arsenal mounting a strong defence of their title. With Arteta’s changes altering the pace of the game, the match turned just before the hour mark. John Brooks saw nothing in the incident that floored Gabriel at a corner, but at the next set-piece penalised Ezri Konsa for wrestling with Dan Ballard, much to Arteta’s fury.

Le Fée had earned a point against Brentford a week earlier with a penalty, but this time his finish was tipped on to the post by David Raya. “We should not talk about the save of the keeper, we should talk about what happened before that,” added Arteta.

“But I loved the save from David, the way the team reacted, the way we go again and we go against everything, but this should never happen, it’s not fair, and I am sad, very sad, in that sense.”.

Raya also denied Nordi Mukiele from close range when Granit Xhaka’s expertly taken free-kick found his team-mate in front of goal. Sunderland have their own European campaign starting on Thursday and will start with confidence after pushing the champions all the way.

Sources indicate that brooks awarded a penalty in stoppage-time when Saka was brought down by Reinildo Mandava, who was dismissed. “I’m extremely pleased to win again. We had a really tough week, Chelsea, Napoli, winning there and now against a really tough opponent in a difficult place,” added Arteta.

Bukayo Saka wraps up all three points for Arsenal from the spot 🥶📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/UrLyrykwlh.

Mikel Arteta launched a furious attack on referee John Brooks for awarding a penalty against Arsenal and fears similar decisions will cost his team the Premier League title.

Brooks gave a spot-kick for Ezri Konsa tussling with Dan Ballard, although Arteta accused the Sunderland centre-back of a “judo roll”.

Enzo Le Fée’s penalty was saved by David Raya, with Arsenal winning after goals from Bruno Guimarães and Bukayo Saka.

Recent findings suggest that “In my opinion, that is not acceptable. I watched it 20 times,” mentioned Arteta. “And I cannot find a way to understand how you think to give a penalty in that situation or the way the VAR has to intervene.

According to recent reports, “I’m sad that we have to discuss something in such a beautiful game at this level. That has gravity because that changes the course of the season and it can cost you the championship. And at this level, with all the work that we put in, this cannot happen.

The key question, though, is not whether Rice can do it, but whether he should do it. Sunderland are the latest team tasked with stopping Arsenal, who have begun their title defence in formidable style: they’ve won out of three, including a dominant comeback victory against Chelsea last weekend, and look well equipped to become the first Arsenal team to retain the title since the mid-1930s.

There’s a long way to go, and Arsenal fans will remember how blisteringly they started their last two title defences in 2002-03 and 2004-05, only to ultimately fall short. But right now, they could barely be in better shape. Their fine start to the season came with a Champions League win in Naples, achieved despite a delay to their flight from London.

In a recent development, “I love those challenges,” noted Mikel Arteta. “I try to create them in pre-seasons so when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else.

“Because when it happens, and it can happen, you can miss the flight, the train can be delayed, there’s so much traffic and I don’t want the players, but not only the players, the staff as well, panicking. So when that happens, adapt to it.”.

Arteta has tested his squad in a variety of ways. “[We have] delayed the meals, delayed the transport, taken a different route. We’ve done many things – made the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less beds... because we’re going to have to adapt to different contexts.”.

So far, they’re adapting very well to the context of being the reigning champions.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Michael Carrick has been sacked by Manchester United, with former Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur boss Mauricio Pochettino waiting in the wings as his successor.
  • Just 173 days on from Carrick being given a two-year contract, having guided United to a third-placed finish and back into the Champions League as an interim, the decision to fire him was ratified at a crucial board meeting in Monaco on Wednesday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 05:22 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 07:34 EST, 12 November 2026.

Michael Carrick has been sacked by Manchester United, with former Chelsea and Tottenham Hotspur boss Mauricio Pochettino waiting in the wings as his successor.

Just 173 days on from Carrick being given a two-year contract, having guided United to a third-placed finish and back into the Champions League as an interim, the decision to fire him was ratified at a crucial board meeting in Monaco on Wednesday.

In a recent development, carrick arrived at United's training ground at 7.50am this morning and was dismissed. He left at 10.18am, less than two and a half hours later. He is the first Premier League manager to be sacked this season, followed hours later by bottom-of-the-table Crystal Palace boss Pierre Sage.

Sources indicate that in a statement released at 10.37am, Carrick's sacking was confirmed. United's statement read: 'After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.

Industry observers note that 'Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club. His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.'.

Recent findings suggest that sources close to United say the club's leadership believe their squad of players is far better than the performances and results under Carrick have indicated. They gave the under-fire manager a chance to turn things around against Chelsea, Roma and Aston Villa but ultimately felt the team were not on the right path.

Michael Carrick - pictured arriving at Carrington on Thursday morning - has been sacked after Manchester United's disastrous start to the season.

Carrick was seen leaving the training ground less than two and a half hours later.

USMNT boss Mauricio Pochettino is ready to take over as United's upcoming manager.

Minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, along with the Glazer family, who dialled in virtually from the United States, chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox reached a verdict in the south of France yesterday, all while Carrick remained in limbo back in Manchester.

Carrick took charge of training on Tuesday morning after it had emerged that Berrada and Wilcox were heading to Monaco to recommend his sacking and did so again on Wednesday when it transpired United were closing in on an agreement to bring in Pochettino as his successor.

The current United States national team manager reached a verbal agreement with Man United to take over on Wednesday. United then made a formal approach to US Soccer shortly after, with the club having to trigger the 54-year-old Argentine's £7million release clause.

The final nail in Carrick’s coffin came in Sunday's dramatic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa, which saw United stuck in the relegation zone in 18th position.

The handling of Carrick’s departure has been particularly damning on Ineos and the shot-callers at United, not least given he was given no show of public support when he continued in post following an emergency board meeting after the 3-0 defeat to Bournemouth.

A defeat at Chelsea, in which Lisandro Martinez badly let his manager down by getting sent off, and a win over Roma to go with the draw against Villa, was not enough of a sign that it will turn around for the board to keep faith.

Industry observers note that with Carrick's departure, it pushes the compensation paid out to coaching staff and executives over the last three years under minority owner Ratcliffe and Ineos close to £30million. Buying Pochettino out of his contract with the US national team will cost another £7m. Adding his large coaching staff will take millions more.

Matchgoing supporters will be sad to see Carrick go and made those feelings clear in recent games when he was loudly cheered at the end of matches, with the ire and frustration levelled against players and executives.

Optimism heading into the campaign was sky high given that no team in the Premier League performed better than Carrick's side between January and May.

But that level of success and dominance has long since evaporated after a shambolic start to the current campaign - and it has cost the 45-year-old his job just five months after the ink dried on a upcoming deal.

It has been a season in which United won just three matches, one of which came against Azerbaijani minnows FK Sabah, and are yet to keep a clean sheet in the league all season.

A season in which club captain Bruno Fernandes publicly questioned his manager's tactics and Martinez eviscerated the hierarchy for hanging Carrick and the players out to dry. Fernandes was even dropped for the first time in five years for the Bournemouth humiliation.

Questions will continue to be asked of those upstairs, with Berrada and Wilcox now on to their third permanent manager this year alone and their fourth in their tenure having burned through Erik ten Hag, Ruben Amorim and Carrick since taking control of football operations in February 2024.

It means Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox (pictured on Thursday morning) need a third manager this year as INEOS' running of the football club comes under scrutiny once more.

Sunday's draw with Aston Villa proved to be the final nail in the coffin for the United boss.

Gary Neville believes Michael Carrick will be 'disgusted' by his Manchester United players.

Amorim lasted 14 months in the role, even in spite of embarrassing defeats to the likes of League Two Grimsby Town, but for Carrick it was a dream job that would run until early November and end in him being unceremoniously dumped at the training ground by Wilcox.

Industry observers note that carrick vowed after the Villa draw that he wouldn’t walk away and took on a spiky side when quizzed on his future by reporters. After a week of shame against the board, he has finally been put out of his misery.

Carrick leaves with a record of 14 wins - 12 of which came last season, prior to being made permanent manager - six draws and eight defeats, including exiting this season's Carabao Cup at the first hurdle against Brighton at Old Trafford.

Now it looks set to be Pochettino’s challenge to turn this massively underperforming squad around, something former United star Gary Neville believes is a mightily difficult task given the 'unprofessional' squad the newly introduced man will inherit.

According to recent reports, 'They've teased him, haven't they? They've conned [Carrick] for a few months. They have, they've conned him,' Neville said on his Sky Sports podcast recently.

Recent findings suggest that 'Honestly, he would never say this publicly because he's got class. I can say it for him though.

'He'll look at those players with disgust. Some of them, he'll be disgusted with some of those players.

'A few of them aren't that professional. I live in Manchester. Some of them aren't that professional. So I've got no time for them.

'There's a few of them that don't go to bed at the right time, don't eat the right things, don't think about Manchester United every single minute of every day, and aren't living and breathing this football club as they should be - and as professionals should.

'Why? Because it's gone to their heads. They are nothing, some of those players.

Sources indicate that 'He's not been able to get a tune out of them and they've turned on him. I know that because if Bruno has turned on him publicly, with that little statement, imagine what they're like behind the scenes.

In a recent development, 'If that's your captain saying that, imagine what they're saying in the dressing room behind closed doors when no one's listening. That's horrific.'.

Comme le souligne la dernière édition du Progrès, le Musée des Verts a décroché un nouveau record d'affluence le 24 octobre dernier à l'occasion de la réception du FC Nantes. 974 personnes l'ont en effet visité ce jour-là, pour le plus grand bonheur de son responsable Laurent Chastellière, dont le quotidien régional a recueilli les propos amusés.

Sources indicate that "Les jours de match, la visite du stade et/ou du musée et le repas au salon 1933 ont trouvé leur rythme de croisière. "On était complet pour les repas pour le match contre Nantes. Depuis septembre, on a changé le menu et ça fonctionne. Avant le match contre Laval, une jeune femme a demandé à son compagnon de l'épouser. Lui avait prévu de le faire pour le réveillon mais elle l'a devancé ! (rires)".

Coprésident du GFA Rumilly Vallières (N1), le réputé fromager Luc Chabert explique au Dauphiné Libéré pourquoi il est si content d'affronter les Verts demain après-midi à Annecy. Extraits.

"Mon père Gérard partait à Geoffroy-Guichard les soirs de Coupe d’Europe. Il était même présent à Glasgow en 1976, il est rentré 4 jours après ! On a toujours vécu avec le maillot vert à la maison. Mon père était président de l’ES Vallières, on jouait en vert. L’origine de la couleur du maillot, c’est l’ASSE. Donc, petit, j’ai baigné dans le vert entre l’ASSE et Vallières. Je crois que c’était la première fois que nous tombions dans le même chapeau que Saint-Étienne. Quand j’ai vu le groupe, j’ai envoyé un SMS à mon fils, Edgar, lui aussi supporter des Verts. Depuis le temps qu’on rêvait de jouer l’ASSE en Coupe de France, notre rêve s’est réalisé !

Recent findings suggest that on a eu des super relations avec les dirigeants stéphanois pour l’organisation du match. Les planètes se sont alignées. Sans le FC Annecy, nous n’aurions pas pu organiser un tel rendez-vous. Et sans la complicité de l’ASSE, on n’aurait pas pu jouer le dimanche après-midi. Ils seront très bien accueillis. Le match, on va le jouer pour le gagner, c’est une certitude. Surtout, on va le vivre pleinement car on n’a aucune pression. On accueillera quoi qu’il arrive le résultat avec fierté et la satisfaction du travail bien fait. Et si l’aventure continue, on sera les plus heureux.".
